latin: अन्नभोगोऽयमधुना द्वयोरन्यो निगद्यते । बान्धवान्मण्डपाधीशान्सामन्तान् मान्यकान् भटान् ॥ ४२ ॥ आश्रितान् सुहृदो भृत्यान् गीतवाद्यविशारदान् । आहूय स्वोचिते स्थाने निर्वेश्याग्रे तु भोजयेत् ॥ ४३ ॥ पुत्रैः पौत्रैः प्रपौत्रैश्च सह भुञ्जीत पार्थिवः । भोज्यं भक्ष्यं तथा पेयं लेह्यं चोष्यं तथैव च ॥ ४४ ॥ इति पञ्चविधं हृद्यं पथ्यं भुञ्जीत भूपतिः । रक्तशालिर्महाशालिर्गन्धशालिः कलिङ्गकः ॥ ४५ ॥ मुण्डशालिः स्थूलशालिः सूक्ष्मशालिः सषष्टिकः । रक्तत्वाद्रक्तशालिः स्यान्महाशालिर्महाकृतिः ॥ ४६ ॥ सुगन्धिर्गन्धशालिः स्यात्कलिङ्गोत्थः कलिङ्गकः । शूकशून्यो मुण्डशालिः स्थूलशालिस्तदाकृतिः ॥ ४७ ॥ सौक्ष्म्यात्तु सूक्ष्मशालिः स्याद्द्विमासः षष्टिकः स्मृतः । एतान् शालीन् पृथक् सर्वान्मुसलैर्वितुषीकृतान् ॥ ४८ ॥ निक्षिप्य तण्डुलान् पट्टे विसृजेत्कणकांस्ततः । पाषाणमृत्तिकाशालीतृणपर्णं तुषं तथा ॥ ४९ ॥
english: This enjoyment of food, the other of the two [under discussion], is now declared. Having summoned kinsmen, the superintendents of the dining pavilion, feudatory lords, men who are to be honoured, soldiers, dependants, friends, servants, and those expert in song and instrumental music, and having seated each in the place proper to him, he should have them eat first. The lord of the earth should eat together with his sons, his grandsons, and his great-grandsons. *Bhojya* — solid food that is eaten; *bhakṣya* — food that is chewed; and likewise *peya* — what is drunk; *lehya* — what is licked; and *coṣya* — what is sucked: food of these five kinds, agreeable and wholesome, the king should eat. [The rices are] *raktaśāli*, *mahāśāli*, *gandhaśāli*, *kaliṅgaka*, *muṇḍaśāli*, *sthūlaśāli*, *sūkṣmaśāli*, and the *ṣaṣṭika* along with them. From its redness it is *raktaśāli*; the *mahāśāli* is of great form; the *gandhaśāli* is the fragrant one; the *kaliṅgaka* is what comes from Kaliṅga; the *muṇḍaśāli* is without an awn; the *sthūlaśāli* is of that [thick] shape; from its fineness it is the *sūkṣmaśāli*; and the *ṣaṣṭika* is reckoned a two-month [rice]. All these rices, each kind separately, are to be husked with pestles. Having put the grains on a board, he should then cast out the *kaṇaka*s [grit and broken grains], and likewise stone, earth, rice-straw, leaf, and husk —

latin: यत्नाद्विकृष्यापनयेद्दासीभिस्तण्डुलस्थितान् । अखण्डान् शोधितानेव क्षालितान् बहुशो जलैः ॥ १३५० ॥ तण्डुलान् कुन्दसङ्काशांस्तोयान्तर्धारितांश्चिरम् । स्थाल्यां ताम्रकृतायां वा मृज्जातायामथापि वा ॥ ५१ ॥ तण्डुलत्रिगुणं तोयं निक्षिपेच्च पिधापयेत् । वाससा शशिशुभ्रेण धौतेन च घनेन च ॥ ५२ ॥ चुल्यां निधाय निर्धूमे वह्नौ तत् काथयेज्जलम् । सुतप्ते बुद्बुदोपेते स्वल्पबाष्पसमन्विते ॥ ५३ ॥ तण्डुलानावपेत्स्थाल्यां दर्व्या च परिघट्टयेत् । सिक्थं विमर्द्य वीक्षेत वारं वारं विचक्षणः ॥ ५४ ॥ मृदूभूते च तत्सिक्थे किञ्चिद्वा कणगर्भिते । तत्र दुग्धं घृतं वापि निक्षिप्योत्तारयेत्ततः ॥ ५५ ॥ स्थाल्यास्ये पिटकं दत्त्वा मण्डं तं स्रावयेद्गुणी । ईषदुद्धरितं मण्डमूष्मणा परिशोषयेत् ॥ ५६ ॥
english: — with care, by means of the maidservants, he should draw out and remove the things lodged in the grain. [This half-verse completes the sentence begun at 1349.] The grains unbroken, thoroughly cleaned, washed many times with water, white as the *kunda* jasmine, and held a long while under water: in a pot made of copper, or else of clay, he should put water three times the rice, and have it covered with a cloth white as the moon, washed, and thick. Setting it on the stove, he should boil that water on a smokeless fire. When the water is thoroughly hot, covered with bubbles, and giving off a little steam, he should strew the rice into the pot and stir it about with a ladle. The discerning man should crush a grain and inspect it again and again. When that grain has gone soft, or still holds a little core, he should put milk into it, or else ghee, and then take it off the fire. Setting a woven lid over the mouth of the pot, the skilled man should let the *māṇḍa* [the starchy cooking water] run off; and the little *māṇḍa* that is left behind he should dry away in the residual heat. [The edition prints *udharitam* here and suggests reading *udveritam*; neither is wholly clear, but the sense is the small quantity of *māṇḍa* not poured off.]

latin: एवं भक्तं सुपक्वं यद्राजयोग्यं तदुत्तमम् । राजमुद्गास्तथा पीता निष्पावाश्चणका अपि ॥ ५७ ॥ कृष्णाढक्यस्तथा माषा मसूरा राजमाषकाः । सूपकर्मणि सप्तैते नियोज्याः सूपकारकैः ॥ ५८ ॥ दलिताऽदलिताश्चैते पचनीया यथारुचि । चणका राजमाषाश्च मसूरा राजमुद्गकाः ॥ ५९ ॥ घरट्टैर्दलिताः कार्याः पाकार्थं हि विचक्षणैः । किंचिद्दष्टास्तथाढक्यो यन्त्रावर्तैर्द्विधाकृताः ॥ १३६० ॥ विदली च कृताः सम्यक् शूर्पकैर्वितुषीकृताः । स्थाल्यां शीतोदकं क्षिप्त्वा विदलैः सममानतः ॥ ६१ ॥ आवपेद्विदलान्पश्चाच्चुल्यामारोपयेत्ततः । मृद्वग्निपच्यमानेऽन्तर्हिङ्गुतोयं विनिक्षिपेत् ॥ ६२ ॥ वर्णार्थं रंजनीचूर्णमीषत्तत्र नियोजयेत् । मुहुर्मुहुःक्षिपेत्तोयं यावत्पाकस्य पूर्णता ॥ ६३ ॥ सुश्लक्ष्णं सैन्धवं कृत्वा विंशत्यंशेन निक्षिपेत् । वर्णतः स्वादतो गन्धान्मार्दवाल्लाघवादपि ॥ ६४ ॥ एवं विदलपाकस्य सम्यक्सिद्धिरुदाहृता । निष्पावा मेचकाढक्यो हिङ्गुना परिवर्जिताः ॥ ६५ ॥ अभिन्नाः पूर्ववत् पाच्या हरिद्राचूर्णकं विना । मसूरमाषपाकेषु हिङ्गुतोयं विनिक्षिपेत् ॥ ६६ ॥
english: Rice cooked well in this way, which is fit for a king, is the best. *Rājamudga*, and likewise *pītā*, *niṣpāva*, and chickpeas too; black *āḍhakī*, and *māṣa*, lentils, *rājamāṣa*: these seven are to be employed by soup-cooks in the making of soup. [The list as printed yields eight names; *pītā*, "the yellow one", is probably an epithet of the *rājamudga* rather than a pulse of its own, since the seven that recur below do not include it.] These are to be cooked split or unsplit, according to taste. Chickpeas, *rājamāṣa*, lentils, and *rājamudga* are to be made split with querns by the discerning, for the sake of cooking; and the *āḍhakī*s, bruised a little, are made twofold by the turnings of the mill. And when they have been properly made into split halves, they are freed of husk with winnowing-baskets. Having put cold water into the pot, equal in measure to the split pulse, he should strew the pulse in, and then set it on the stove. While it is cooking on a gentle fire he should throw asafoetida-water into it. For the sake of colour he should employ a little turmeric powder in it. Again and again he should add water, until the cooking is complete. Making rock-salt very fine, he should put it in at a twentieth part. By colour, by taste, by aroma, by softness, and by lightness too — thus is declared the proper perfection of the cooking of split pulse. *Niṣpāva*s and dark *āḍhakī*s, kept free of asafoetida and unsplit, are to be cooked as before, without turmeric powder. In the cooking of lentils and *māṣa* he should throw in asafoetida-water.

latin: इतरः पूर्ववत् कार्यः पाकः पाकविचक्षणैः । प्रक्षालितान्वरान्मुद्गान् समतोये विनिक्षिपेत् ॥ ६७ ॥ चुल्यां मृद्वग्निना पाकः कर्तव्यः सूपकारकैः । पच्यमानेषु मुद्गेषु हिङ्गुवारि विनिक्षिपेत् ॥ ६८ ॥ आर्द्रकस्य च खण्डानि सूक्ष्माणि च विनिक्षिपेत् । वार्ताकं पाटितं तैलभृष्टं तत्र विनिक्षिपेत् ॥ ६९ ॥ तैलभृष्टा मृदूभूताः क्षिपेद्वा बिसचक्रिकाः । बीजानि वा प्रियालस्य क्षिप्त्वा दर्व्या विवर्तयेत् ॥ १३७० ॥ पुनः पुनः क्षिपेत्तोयं स्तोकं स्तोकं विचक्षणः । केचिदिच्छन्ति रुच्यर्थं मेषमांसस्य खण्डकान् ॥ ७१ ॥ वृक्कान्वापि द्विधा भिन्नान्मेदसः शकलानि वा । मुहुः सूपे सुनिष्पन्ने चूर्णितं मरिचं क्षिपेत् ॥ ७२ ॥
english: The other preparation is to be made as before by those skilled in cooking. He should put washed, choice mung beans into an equal measure of water. The cooking is to be done on the stove with a gentle fire by the soup-cooks. While the mung beans are cooking he should throw in asafoetida-water, and he should also throw in small pieces of fresh ginger. Eggplant, split and fried in oil, he should throw in there. Or he may put in lotus-stem discs, fried in oil and gone soft, or the kernels of the *priyāla*; having put them in, he should turn them about with the ladle. Again and again the discerning man should add water, a little at a time. Some, for the sake of relish, want pieces of sheep's flesh, or kidneys split in two, or slices of fat. When the soup is well done he should repeatedly put in powdered pepper.

latin: उत्तार्य नागरं चूर्णं क्षिप्त्वा दर्व्या विघट्टयेत् । श्यामाककङ्गुनीवारगन्धशालिसुतण्डुलैः ॥ ७३ ॥ सरवेष्टिकसेवाकैर्दिवसैर्लघुविस्तृतैः । चिरप्रसूतमहिषीपयसा पायसं पचेत् ॥ ७४ ॥ पायसं लेहने योग्यं स्वादुगन्धं मनोहरम् । गोधूमाः क्षालिता शुभ्राः शोषिता रविरश्मिभिः ॥ ७५ ॥
english: Having taken it off the fire, he should put in powdered dry ginger and stir it about with the ladle. [This half-verse completes the mung soup of the preceding passage.] With the fine grains of *śyāmāka*, *kaṅgu*, *nīvāra*, and fragrant *śāli*, and with *sara*, *veṣṭika*, and *sevāka*, spread out thin over [some] days, he should cook a *pāyasa* in the milk of a buffalo that calved long ago. [The first half of this verse is corrupt: the edition prints *sara-veṣṭika-sevākaiḥ* and suggests *veṣṭita* for *veṣṭika*; the three terms cannot be identified with confidence.] The *pāyasa* is fit for licking, sweet-smelling, and delightful. Wheat grains, washed, white, dried by the rays of the sun —

latin: घरट्टैश्चूर्णिताः श्लक्ष्णाश्चालन्या वितुषीकृताः । गोधूमचूर्णकं श्लक्ष्णं किंचित्घृतविमिश्रितम् ॥ ७६ ॥ लवणेन च संयुक्तं क्षीरनीरेण पिण्डितम् । सुमहत्यां काष्ठपात्र्यां करास्फालैर्विमर्दयेत् ॥ ७७ ॥ मर्दितं चिक्कणीभूतं गोलकान्परिकल्पयेत् । स्नेहाभ्यक्तैः करतलैः शालिचूर्णैर्विरूक्षितान् ॥ ७८ ॥ प्रसारयेत्गोलकांस्तान् करसञ्चारवर्तनैः । विस्तृता मण्डकाः श्लक्ष्णाः सितपट्टसमप्रभाः ॥ ७९ ॥ प्रयत्नान्निक्षिपेत्तज्ज्ञस्तप्तखर्परमस्तके । पक्वांश्चापनयेच्छीघ्रं यावत्कार्ष्ण्यं न जायते ॥ १३८० ॥
english: — ground fine with querns and freed of bran with a sieve. [This half-verse completes the sentence begun at 1375.] The fine wheat flour, mixed with a little ghee, joined with salt, and made into a lump with milk and water, he should knead in a very large wooden vessel with slaps of the hands. When it has been kneaded and has turned smooth and glossy, he should form it into balls; and with palms smeared with fat, the balls dusted dry with rice flour, he should spread those balls out by passing and turning them with the hands. Spread broad, the *maṇḍaka*s are smooth, of a lustre equal to white silk. He who knows this should lay them carefully on the crown of a heated *kharpara* [earthenware griddle], and should take them off quickly once they are cooked, before any blackness arises.

latin: चतस्रश्च चतस्रश्च घटिता मण्डका वराः । गोलान्प्रसारितान्पाणावङ्गारेषु विनिक्षिपेत् ॥ ८१ ॥ अङ्गारपोलिकाः शस्ताः किंचित्कृष्णत्वमागताः । गोलकान्पिष्टकालिप्तान् पेषण्या तान्प्रसारयेत् ॥ ८२ ॥ सुतप्ततापनिक्षिप्तानीषत्पक्वान्विवर्तयेत् । कर्परेऽपि पचेदेवं पोलिकानामयं क्रमः ॥ ८३ ॥
english: *Maṇḍaka*s fitted together four and four are the best. [This half-verse closes the preceding *maṇḍaka* passage.] Balls spread out on the palm he should throw among the embers. *Aṅgārapolikā*s [ember-*polikā*s] are at their best when they have taken on a little blackness. Balls smeared with flour he should spread out with a grinding-stone; thrown onto a thoroughly heated *tāpana* [griddle-plate], he should turn them over when they are a little cooked. On a *karpara* too he may cook them in this same way. This is the procedure for *polikā*s.

latin: तैलपूर्णकटाहे तु सुतप्ते सोहलां पचेत् । उत्तानपाकसंसिद्धाः कठिनाः सोहला मताः ॥ ८४ ॥ तैलमग्नाः पीतवर्णा मृद्वः पाहलिकाः स्मृताः ।
english: In a cauldron full of oil, thoroughly heated, he should cook the *sohalā*. Brought to completion by cooking face-up, the *sohalā*s are held to be firm. Sunk in the oil, yellow in colour, and soft — these are known as *pāhalikā*s.

latin: तनुप्रसारितान्गोलान्ताप्यां स्नेहेन पाचितान् ॥ ८५ ॥ उपर्युपरि निक्षिप्ताः पत्रिका विपचेत्सुधीः ।
english: Balls spread out thin and cooked with fat on the *tāpī* [griddle], laid one above another — the wise man should cook them as *patrikā*s.

latin: गोधूमचूर्णादुद्धृत्य शूर्पेणाभ्याहतान् कणान् ॥ ८६ ॥ दुग्धाक्तान् घृतपक्वांश्च सितया च विमिश्रितान् । एलामरिचचूर्णेन युक्तान्कासारसंज्ञितान् ॥ ८७ ॥
english: The coarse grains taken up out of the wheat flour and beaten out with a winnowing-basket, moistened with milk, cooked in ghee, mixed with white sugar, and joined with powder of cardamom and pepper: these are called *kāsāra*.
Having wrapped them [the *kāsāra* grains] up completely in a ball of dough, he should cook the *udumbara*s with oil.

latin: उत्क्वाथ्य विदलान् पिष्ट्वा चणकप्रभृतीन् शुभान् ॥ ८८ ॥ हिङ्गुसैन्धवसंयुक्तान् शर्करापरिमिश्रितान् । मरिचैलाविचूर्णेन युक्तान्गोलकवेष्टितान् ॥ ८९ ॥ किंचित्प्रसारिते तैले पूरिका विपचेच्छुभाः । एवं ताप्यां पचेदन्याः पूरिकाश्च विचक्षणः ॥ १३९० ॥
english: Having boiled and ground fine excellent split pulses, chickpeas and the rest, joined with asafoetida and rock-salt, mixed with sugar, joined with powder of pepper, cardamom, and the like, and wrapped in a ball of dough: in oil spread a little he should cook fine *pūrikā*s. In this same way the discerning man may cook other *pūrikā*s on the *tāpī* [griddle]. [At 1389c the edition prints *maricailāvi-cūrṇena*; the sense requires *maricailādi-cūrṇena*, "with powder of pepper, cardamom, and the like".]
